status-text.preview-mode: The first steps are not finished: your rules are not working yet.
status-text.checking-status: Checking whether the service is reachable and whether your rules are being applied.
status-text.no-active-policy: Your rules are not being applied right now.
status-text.service-unavailable: The background service is not reachable: rules cannot be applied or changed until it is back.

setup-state.allowed: Action is available in the current setup state.
setup-state.soft-guided: Available; finishing the first steps first is recommended.
setup-state.blocked-until-wizard-completion: Available once the first steps are finished.

tray.preview-only-note: This action is not available yet.

add-rule.title: Add rule
add-rule.load-failed: Could not read your rules from the service, so nothing was added. Check that the service is running.
add-rule.on-other-route: {value} is already in your rules, on the connection {route}.
add-rule.on-other-route-many: {count} of these are already in your rules, on the other connection.
add-rule.already-denied: {value} is already denied in your rules.
add-rule.already-denied-many: {count} of these are already denied in your rules.
add-rule.on-a-route-many: {count} of these are already in your rules, on one of the connections.
add-rule.on-other-route-or-denied-many: {count} of these are already in your rules, on the other connection or denied.
add-rule.added-awaits-confirmation: Rule added: {value} → {route}. Not in use yet: it touches a protected system program — confirm it in the rules list.
add-rule.added-disabled: Rule added, switched off: {value} → {route}. It does not route anything until you switch it on.
add-rule.added-deny-disabled: Rule added, switched off: deny {value}. It does not deny anything until you switch it on.
add-rule.changed-elsewhere: Your rules were changed elsewhere in the meantime, so nothing was added. Open the main window and add the rule there.
add-rule.undo-load-failed: Could not read your rules from the service, so nothing was undone. Check that the service is running.
add-rule.undo-changed: The rule has been changed since, so nothing was undone.
add-rule.undone: Undone: the rules are as they were.

suggestions.silence-body: New addresses will not be offered for as long as you choose. They keep collecting under Suggested addresses.

tooltip.service-not-installed: Service not installed — click to install
tooltip.no-updates: The service is running, but the program is not getting news from it
tooltip.no-rules-applied: NetRuleRouter — your rules are not working yet
tooltip.contract-skew: Program and service versions differ — rules cannot be changed for now

auto-rules.body-multi: Found addresses that {count} of the sites you routed need.
auto-rules.route-line-primary: They will go through the main connection.
auto-rules.route-line-secondary: They will go through the additional connection.
auto-rules.empty: No addresses to suggest right now.
auto-rules.none-pending: Nothing is waiting to be added right now.
auto-rules.unchecked-declined: Unchecked rows will be declined; you can bring them back later in the app.
auto-rules.body-blocked-multi: Connections to {count} sites keep failing on the main connection.

auto-rules-mode-confirm.title: Turn on “Apply automatically”?
auto-rules-mode-confirm.body: From now on NetRuleRouter will add suggested addresses to your rules files by itself, without asking. You can undo this anytime in Settings → Routing behavior, by switching back to “Suggest only”.

rules-drift.body: The rules in your files are not the ones in use right now. Apply them, or open the program to see the difference.

merged.title: {count} connections blocked
merged.body: Tick the addresses to send through the additional connection.

reason.route-unavailable: The connection these addresses should go through is down right now, so none of them open. This is one notice for the whole connection.
reason.blocked-by-rule: A rule denies this address directly.
reason.ipv6-blocked: With leak protection set to Everything, IPv6 goes out only through the additional connection, and this IPv6 address could not. No rule blocked it — the switch is in Settings.
reason.dns-lockdown: This app tried to reach a public DNS resolver of its own instead of the one NetRuleRouter provides, and encrypted-DNS blocking closed it. No rule blocked it — the switch is in Settings, under Routing behavior.
reason.unattributed: NetRuleRouter blocked this address, but could not tell what exactly stopped it.

route-confirm.title-many: Send {count} addresses through the additional connection (e.g. VPN)?

snooze.body-many: Stop asking about these {count} addresses for a while.

settings-lost.body: This happens after the service was reinstalled or its data was reset. Settings missing: {count}.

tray.settings-restore-failed: Your settings could not be restored. Open the app to try again.

pause.title: Turn off rules
pause.body: Your rules and leak protection stop for the time you choose and come back on their own.
pause.failed: Could not turn the rules off:

verify-verdicts.list: Rules and the connection they would move to

local-networks.body: {cidr} on {adapter} stays reachable while leak protection blocks traffic. Keep it that way?
local-networks.body-open: Your home network's IPv6 addresses {cidr} on {adapter} are closed while leak protection blocks traffic. Open them to devices on this network?

vpn-client-trust.tray-body: {apps} looks like a VPN client, but it is not installed in a protected program folder. Open NetRuleRouter to confirm it, or leak protection keeps blocking it while the additional connection is down.

vpn-gateway-trust.tray-body: A VPN is waiting for your answer in the NetRuleRouter window: leak protection stopped it from reaching its server {addresses}.

service-lost.body: The NetRuleRouter service stopped unexpectedly, so your rules are not applied. Start it again, or restore network access if the connection is cut.
